en.title: GTA 6 Fans Plague Nudist Resort with Fake Reviews After Leaks
en.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans have mistakenly targeted a real-life nudist resort with a barrage of fake reviews, believing it inspired an in-game location. The resort's owner has spoken out against the 'coordinated series of fabricated posts.'
en.body:
The anticipation for **Grand Theft Auto 6** is reaching fever pitch, and it seems some fans have taken their sleuthing a step too far. Following leaks that showcased an in-game nudist resort, players have identified **Cypress Cove Nudist Resort** in Kissimmee, Florida, as the apparent real-world inspiration. However, this connection has led to the resort being inundated with fake, GTA 6-themed reviews on platforms like Google.

The owner of Cypress Cove has publicly addressed the situation, stating that the influx of reviews is a "coordinated series of fabricated posts using GTA VI references." They explicitly noted that the resort "is located in Florida — not Leonida" (the fictional state where GTA 6 is set). The resort has documented these reviews and has stated, "we will not pay" and "we will not negotiate" in response to alleged extortion attempts related to the fake reviews, confirming that the activity is being reported through appropriate channels.

## Nudist Resort Denies Game Inspiration

This unexpected online harassment comes as a shock to the owners, who are now dealing with a wave of negative attention that has nothing to do with their actual services. The reviews, reportedly referencing game characters like "Jason" and "Lucia," as well as in-game elements like firearms and binoculars, are entirely unrelated to the resort's operations. The owner's statement emphasizes the absurdity of the situation, noting "a nudist resort DENYING exposure?" while trying to manage the digital onslaught.

## Fan Dedication and Real-World Impact

Fans tracking down real-world locations that may have inspired video game settings is a common practice, often leading to positive engagement. However, in this instance, the fervent belief in a connection has led to a negative outcome for a small business. It underscores the immense power of online communities and how quickly passion can spill over into unintended consequences. While the leaks themselves showcased elements like "more penises than you could count" and "naked bullet hail," the resort is clearly keen to distance itself from such associations, emphasizing its reality as a peaceful retreat.

## What's Next

Rockstar Games has yet to officially comment on the leaks or any potential real-world inspirations for **Grand Theft Auto 6** locations. The resort owners are continuing to monitor and report the fraudulent reviews as they work to mitigate the impact on their business.

content_raw: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans believe its nudist resort was inspired by a real-life location, and its owners are already being bombarded with problematic reviews. As if there was ever any doubt, GTA 6 fans are all over Rockstar Games' new video game. They've measured oxygen levels in hopes of predicting big reveals , showed up for Netflix announcements , and now, they've discovered what they believe was the inspiration for one of the many locations they'll visit in-game this November: Kissimmee, Florida's Cypress Cove Nudist Resort (via GamesRadar ). Fans tracking down the locations behind some of their favorite video game levels is nothing new; Arc Raiders fans did something similar in January. But where the sleuthing for some games has often resulted in real-world positivity, Cypress Cove Nudist Resort isn't enjoying the increased visibility brought by GTA 6. "For anyone wondering about the suddenly recurring references to 'Jason Duval,' 'Lucia,' binoculars, a pool, firearms, and other suspiciously similar details — those are references to Grand Theft Auto VI," the site owner said in response to just one of the many reviews that have shown up on the Cypress Cove Nudist Resort Google page recently. "Yes. A video game." The owner, which has already taken what action it can against the reviews, said the influx of reviews is a "coordinated series of fabricated posts using GTA VI references." They then allege that some posts were followed by requests that the rest "pay money to have the reviews changed or removed." Their message continued, stating, "we will not pay" and "we will not negotiate," confirming it had "documented the reviews and the request for payment." It added, "This activity is being reported through the appropriate channels." "For our actual guests and anyone researching Cypress Cove: please understand that these posts do not describe genuine guest experiences at our resort," the Cypress Cove Nudist Resort's Google representative said. "And to whoever is behind them: We appreciate the commitment to the GTA storyline, but Cypress Cove is located in Florida — not Leonida." GTA 6 fans first caught wind of an in-game nudist resort not from Rockstar but from leaks that polluted the internet last month. Despite the lack of an official showing, early footage provided enough information for watchers to piece together how the developer might have pulled from the real world for its upgraded version of Vice City. Whether this is the location Rockstar looked to or not, it seems that, for the most part, GTA 6-related reviews have been scrubbed from the Google page, but the site owner's message can still be found on a few of the more suspicious messages. These include references to leaks, such as a man who "pulled out his binoculars." One posted yesterday directly referenced GTA 6, saying, "Will be trying to book a reservation on Nov. 19th.
